commentary: This week the money in AI hardware is rotating toward the makers of servers and the tools that build chips, and away from the priciest, most crowded names. We're keeping our Dell position — it's the cheapest, strongest player in AI servers, its story is still working, and rival Super Micro just fell 29% in a month, pushing more business Dell's way. We're adding Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE), which trades at roughly half Dell's valuation while analysts are sharply raising their profit estimates after a record quarter and the completion of its big Juniper networking deal. We deliberately passed on AMD and Astera Labs for now: both are excellent businesses but report earnings within a few weeks, and buying right before an earnings 'coin flip' is a bet we'd rather not make. Prices are getting a little stretched and inflation ticked back up, so we're staying selective — the plan is to own cheap, improving companies and let the winners run.
